title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). G is a discrete commutative group whose finite-index subgroups M_i are free Z-modules of finite type, for example G ≃ Z^n. Its 'pro-schematic envelope' End(G) over Spec Z sits in the exact sequence (51): 1 → End°(G) → lim End(G) → Ĝ_{S0} → 1. The neutral component is End°(G) = lim_i V(M_i), with V(M) = Spec Sym(M^∨) the vector group of M, and the transition maps come from the inclusions M_i ⊂ M_j.

This page computes End°(G) explicitly.

(1) Reduction to rank one. The system of the M_i is cofinal with the system n·M_0 for any fixed M_0 among them, so End°(G) ≃ End°(M_0). A Z-basis of M_0 then gives (54): End°(G) ≃ End°(M_0) ≃ (End°(Z))^n =: (E^1)^n.

(2) The rank-one object (55). E^1 = End°(Z) = lim_n V(nZ). The dual of nZ is (1/n)Z, so V(nZ) = Spec Z[T/n]. The colimit of the rings Z[T/n] is the subring of Q[T] generated over Z by all T^k/n, which is Z + T·Q[T]. Hence E^1 ≃ Spec(Z + TQ[T]). Equivalently, E^1 = lim (E^1, n): the marginal note says the transition (E^1, mn) → (E^1, n) is multiplication by m, i.e. a tower of copies of G_a.

(3) Functor of points (56). A ring map Z + TQ[T] → A is the same as a family (x_n), with x_n the image of T/n, satisfying x_n = m·x_{mn}. So E^1(A) = lim(A, ·m) = Hom_Z(Q, A).

(4) The bracketed remark.
- If nA = 0 for some n, then E^1(A) = 0 (written multiplicatively as {1}). Such an n exists exactly when A ⊗ Q = 0, i.e. when all residue characteristics are positive.
- If all residue characteristics are 0, then A is a Q-algebra and E^1(A) ≃ A.

Consequences, matching the previous page:
- Z + TQ[T] is torsion-free, hence flat over Z, but not of finite type.
- Its fibre over F_p is Spec F_p, because Q is divisible; its generic fibre is G_{a,Q}.
- So End°(G) is the flat, non-finite-type group scheme over Z with trivial closed fibres and generic fibre G_{a,Q}^n.

Purpose: this is a step in describing the 'enveloppe pro-schématique' over Z of discrete groups (abelian case first). The next page passes to a universal characterization of the envelope via unipotent and quasi-unipotent homomorphisms Γ_S → G. It belongs to the Longue Marche programme of algebraic envelopes of fundamental groups over Z.
errors: The bracket claims 'nA = 0 ⟺ residue characteristics divide n'. Only ⇒ holds. If all residue characteristics divide n, then n is nilpotent and n^k·A = 0 for some k, but nA = 0 can fail (A = Z/p^2). This is harmless: the correct criterion for E^1(A) = 0 is A ⊗ Q = 0, i.e. some N with N·1_A = 0.

'Si A est de car. 0 alors E^1(A) ≃ A' is correct only if 'car. 0' means all residue characteristics are 0, i.e. A is a Q-algebra. For A = Z (char 0 in the naive sense), E^1(Z) = Hom(Q, Z) = 0 ≠ Z. In general E^1(A) = Hom_Z(Q, A).
Minor: the isomorphisms (54) are non-canonical, since they depend on the choice of M_0 and of a basis. The text acknowledges this.

ideas.what: Neutral component of the pro-schematic envelope of a free abelian group of rank n over Z, computed as lim of vector groups V(nM) and identified with (E^1)^n
ideas.modern_name: Pro-algebraic / affine-group-scheme envelope (schematization) of discrete groups over Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pro-unipotent completion over Q: Malcev, Quillen, Deligne. Over Z: Toën ('Le problème de la schématisation de Grothendieck', 2020), Ekedahl and others in various forms
ideas.where_published: The schematization problem is raised in Pursuing Stacks and in letters. This explicit computation over Z appears only in these Longue Marche follow-up notes, as far as known

ideas.what: Ring computation colim_n Z[T/n] = Z + TQ[T]
ideas.modern_name: Standard example of a non-noetherian ring, used as a subring of Q[T]

ideas.what: Group scheme Spec(Z+TQ[T]) represents A ↦ Hom_Z(Q, A) = lim(A, ×m); it is flat over Z with trivial closed fibres and generic fibre G_a
ideas.modern_name: Representability of Hom(Q, -); limit of a tower of G_a's under multiplication maps (a 'vector-group analogue' of a Tate/universal-cover construction)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly computes the identity component of his pro-schematic envelope of Z^n over Spec Z. It is (Spec(Z+TQ[T]))^n, representing Hom(Q,-)^n, with trivial fibres at all primes. All the p-adic information sits in the profinite quotient Ĝ_{S0}. This is a concrete structural answer to an integral schematization of discrete groups, decomposed as a characteristic-0 vector part plus a profinite étale part. It is a different object from the integer-valued-polynomial Hopf algebra used in later integral unipotent completions (Toën, Ekedahl).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Recent work on affine stacks and schematic homotopy types over Z uses different integral envelopes. Grothendieck's variant, built from a 'connected component plus profinite completion' extension, could be compared with these. That comparison does not appear to be in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are elementary and essentially correct. Their interest lies in documenting Grothendieck's own construction of an integral pro-schematic envelope of discrete groups (identity component plus profinite quotient), which seems unpublished. The individual facts are folklore.
transcription_corrections: The second label in the display is likely '(54)' continued or a separate number (looks like '(54)'/'(59)'); the following displays are (55) and (56).
The marginal note reads roughly 'où (E^1, mn) → (E^1, n) est la multiplication par m', inserted at (55).
'est le schéma en groupes commutatif [?] plus haut' is more plausibly 'est le schéma en groupes vu plus haut'.
'il existe dans donc un tel n' should read 'il existe donc un tel n'.
In (56) a crossed-out lim symbol precedes the set; the resulting condition is x_n = m·x_{mn} for all m, n ∈ N*.
The first lines are hard to read. They plausibly say that M_0 is one of the M_i, giving an isomorphism (canonical up to the inclusion among the M_i) with End°(M_0).
